articles.title: Bike Crash Sparks Communal Clash in Amroha: House Torched, Several Injured
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Amroha (Uttar Pradesh) – A clash broke out between two communities in Thana Naugawan Sadat area on 18 June after a bike collided with a car. Tensions escalated when members of the Dalit community allegedly vandalised and set fire to the house of a Muslim youth involved in the accident.

body.html:
Amroha (Uttar Pradesh) – A clash broke out between two communities in Thana Naugawan Sadat area on 18 June after a bike collided with a car. Tensions escalated when members of the Dalit community allegedly vandalised and set fire to the house of a Muslim youth involved in the accident. A cotton warehouse was also torched.

Several people from both sides were injured. Police and fire brigade reached the spot swiftly and controlled the situation. Heavy police and PAC deployment continues. FIR has been filed and arrests are expected soon.

articles.title: Insult to Shri Ram: Youth Made to Apologise in Temple After Abusive Post
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: In Uttar Pradesh’s Fatehpur district, a youth named Mohammed Yassir was caught by Hindu organisations after he allegedly abused Lord Shri Ram on Instagram.

body.html:
In Uttar Pradesh’s Fatehpur district, a youth named Mohammed Yassir was caught by Hindu organisations after he allegedly abused Lord Shri Ram on Instagram. In response, the group took Yassir to a nearby temple, applied tilak on his forehead, and made him publicly apologise for his remarks.

The video of the incident has gone viral, sparking debates on religious sensitivity and social media conduct. Police are reportedly aware of the situation and are monitoring developments.

articles.title: Loan Recovery or Lawlessness? Woman Tied to Tree in CM Naidu’s Constituency Over ₹80,000 Debt
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: In a shocking incident from Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu’s own constituency, Kuppam in Andhra Pradesh’s Chittoor district, a woman was tied to a tree after her husband failed to repay a loan.

body.html:
In a shocking incident from Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu’s own constituency, Kuppam in Andhra Pradesh’s Chittoor district, a woman was tied to a tree after her husband failed to repay a loan.

Sirisha, a resident of Narayanapuram village, was allegedly tied with a rope by loan giver Munikannappa and his family in front of her child. Her husband Thimmarayappa had taken a loan of ₹80,000 three years ago and failed to repay it. The couple had since moved away, but Sirisha had returned to the village on Monday to collect a study certificate for her son.

The Kuppam Urban Police rescued her after receiving information. A case has been registered against Munikannappa and his family members. Police have launched an investigation.

articles.title: 🐙 Man or Octopus? Thief Bends Like Rubber to Rob Nagpur Beer Shop — Shocks Police!
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A bizarre theft in Nagpur has left even the police stunned. On the night of June 6, ₹25,000 was stolen from Ramashree Beer Bar under Wathoda Police Station. What seemed like an impossible heist — due to a secure iron grill — turned out to be a jaw-dropping feat of flexibility.

body.html:
A bizarre theft in Nagpur has left even the police stunned. On the night of June 6, ₹25,000 was stolen from Ramashree Beer Bar under Wathoda Police Station. What seemed like an impossible heist — due to a secure iron grill — turned out to be a jaw-dropping feat of flexibility.

CCTV footage revealed a man slipping through the tiny payment opening at the counter — a space meant only for hands. Twisting his body like rubber, the thief entered, grabbed the cash, and exited the same way, without damaging the grill.

The accused, identified as 20-year-old Sheikh Raja Sheikh Baba from Amravati, was arrested on June 13. He confessed not only to this theft but also to multiple two-wheeler thefts in Amravati.

Wathoda Police Inspector Harish Borade confirmed the arrest and said the unique break-in style has become a topic of citywide discussion.
